full_judgment:
4. Defence version in short is that the appellant Abdul Majid was not entrusted with domain over the stamp and stationery, that there was no shortage of stamp and stationery as alleged, that he was never in charge of stamp and stationery, that ex-post master Mr Yousuf and Mr. Matiar Rahman were in charge of stamp and stationery during relevant period as they used to supply stamp and stationery to Sub-Post-Offices as per indent and they were actual custodian of the stamp and stationery during relevant period, that if there be any defalcation in respect of the stamp and stationery, it is the Post Master in charge who should be held responsible for such defalcation, that he is innocent, that he has been falsely implicated in this case at the instance of ex-post master Mr. Matiar Rahman and Mr. Yousuf to screen themselves from criminal liability. On consideration of the evidence on record the learned Special Judge Khulna Division found the appellant to be guilty to the charge framed against him and convicted and sentenced him to the terms as mentioned above. 

 5. The learned counsel Mr. Md. Abdur Rahim appearing on behalf of the appellant has assailed the impugned judgment of the Special Judge on the ground that it is based on misreading of evidence and that the finding of conviction is founded on misappreciation of law. The learned Counsel further urged that in absence of any proof of alleged defalcation, the charge of commission of criminal breach of trusts in respect of the stamp and stationery worth Tk. 67,534/43 paisa cannot stand. In this connection the learned Counsel for the appellant submitted that verification of the stamp and stationery was conducted by informant Yousuf (P.W.1) along with Sultan and Razzaque, Naziruddin, Assistant Superintendent (Investigation) and during such verification a register showing stock of stationery and stamp as stood on 6.7.68 was consulted and a report of such verification was prepared. But no evidence in this regard was produced by the prosecution side. This contention of the learned Counsel appears to be well founded. 

 6. P.W.1 Mr. Yousuf, the then Post Master of Khulna G.P.O., P.W. 2 Sultan, the then Assistant Post Master General and P.W. 4 A. Razzaq, Assistant Post Master were connected with the physical verification of the stamp and stationery of G.P.O. Khulna. Of these three witnesses P.W. 4 A. Razzaq did not say a word of shortage of stamp and stationery. He stated in his evidence that a daily stamp register was checked during verification. P.W. 2 Mr. Sultan Ahmed stated in his evidence that on verification of Register he found short stamp and stationery worth of Tk. 67,534.43 and accordingly he submitted report. P.W. 1 Mr. Yousuf also said verification was made with reference to Register. Thus from the evidence of aforesaid witnesses who held responsible position, it is evident that prior to physical verification, Registers were consulted and a report was prepared. But neither Register nor report showing alleged shortage was produced during trial. Basis of oral testimony of aforesaid witnesses is registers and report said to have been prepared during verification. Thus it is affirmatively proved by admission of the aforesaid three responsible witnesses of postal department that documentary evidence to prove alleged shortage was available at the time of trial, but it is not known why primary documentary evidence was withheld by prosecution during trial. Rule of evidence is that the best evidence which the case in its nature is susceptible should always be given. In other words in each case best available evidence should be produced. Primary evidence is the best or highest evidence. It is that kind of proof which in the eye of law affords the greatest certainty of facts in question. Unless it is shown that production of this evidence is out of party's power, no other proof of fact is generally admitted. In the instant case it has been found that documentary evidence has purposely been withheld with some ulterior motive. In view of legal principle referred above oral testimony to prove shortage of stamp and stationery is inadmissible in evidence. In order to establish charge of criminal breach of trust distinct proof of criminal misappropriation is necessary. But except oral evidence no other evidence has been led to prove criminal misappropriation of stamp and stationery. Thus it is found that distinct proof of alleged misappropriation has not been established in this case. 

 7.  Now it is to be seen if appellant Abdul Majid was entrusted with the domain of the stamp and stationery of G.P.O., Khulna. He stoutly denied entrustment or domain over the property. Informant Mr. Yousuf (P.W. 1) has admitted in his cross-examination that as per provision contained under article 304 of Initial Account Manual, valuable article of post office shall remain in joint custody of post master and Treasurer. He further admits that there is a duty card in which particular duty assigned to an employee is written and the days, chart is to be signed by the Post Master, He further admits that the stamp and stationery being checked by inspection officer once in two months and that it was done in the instant case but no discrepancy in the stock of stamp was detected. Thus it is evident from his deposition that as per rules the post master is the actual custodian of stamp and stationery. P,W. 4 Razzaque the then Assistant Postmaster G.P.O. Khulna has also testified to the fact that the post master is the sole custodian of the stamp and stationery and he stated that stamp and stationery were checked daily. He further stated that is the duty of the post master to check the stamp position on completion of each day's work and according to rules post master is responsible for the shortage of stamp and cash. He further deposed to say that the Deputy Postmaster was in fact in charge of the stamp and stationery as per allocation of the duty. It is also evident from the deposition of P.W. 1 that there is no post in the Manual bearing designation as stamp clerk. P.W. 1 Yousuf further admits per article 370 of Initial Account Rule the postmaster is under legal obligation to check sale proceed after each day's work. Thus from the evidence of the officers of postal department it is abundantly clear that appellant was not entrusted with the domain of the stamp and stationery and consequently charge of criminal misappropriation cannot stand against him. P.W. 1 and P.W. admitted that stamp register used to be maintained by stamp clerk appellant Abdul Majid. But that register bearing Mazid's band writing was not proved during trial to fix up the charge of criminal misappropriation with appellant Mazid. It is established beyond doubt that as per statement made by P.W. 1 Yousuf and P.W. 4 Razzaque post master was actual custodian of the Govt. property and under rules of Postal Manual he is not authorised to entrust its dominion on others. 

 8. It is an essential condition that property which is subject-matter of offence roust have been entrusted to a person. The term entrustment or dominion over the property implies handing over the property far some purpose. The word "entrustment" conveys and includes that person handing over the property must have confidence on the person taking the property so as to create fiduciary relation between them. So strop proof of entrustment of property or dominion over the property to the accused is prerequisite condition to be satisfied for establishing the charge of criminal misappropriation. But evidence on the point is hopelessly lacking. Evidence of the prosecution witness does not throw any light on this point. Rather their evidence disproved entrustment of the property or its dominion on appellant Majid. 

 It also appears that one set of keys of the door of stamp room and the door of the receptacles used to remain with the post master and the other set used to remain in possession of Mr. Abdul Majid, stamp clerk. It is apparent chat the accused Abdul Majid had domain over the stamp papers entrusted to him." But surprisingly no evidence has been referred by Learned Judge in support of this finding. It is nothing but a figment of imagination. In absence of duty chart showing allocation of duty to appellant Majid and Register purported to contain his hand writing the alleged story of entrustment falls through. The learned judge failed to apply correct principle in appreciating evidence in this regard and thus arrived at an erroneous conclusion. In fact be grossly misread evidence. He relied much on moral conviction than on legal testimony. Rule of evidence cannot be departed from because there may be strong conviction of guilt but Judge can not set himself above the law which he himself is to administer or to make it or mound it to suit the need of exigency of particular occasion. Conviction must be based on sufficient evidence and not on moral conviction. Further in this case appellant Majid took up substantive defence referred above and such defence received support from prosecution evidence itself. It is incumbent upon prosecution to establish by definite and clear evidence that case for defence is untrue. But no evidence whatsoever has been led to prove that plea set up by defence side is not wordy of credit. 

 12. Before I part with the record I like to observe that investigating agency during investigation collected inculpatory materials linking ex-postmaster Mr. Yousuf and his predecessor Mr. Matiur Rahman with that criminal appropriation of stamps and stationery of Khulna G.P.O. and accordingly sanction was sought from competent authority for submission of charge-sheet against them. But all attempts of the law enforcing agency to obtain sanction against them ended in failure. Trial Court also felt their complicity in the crime and ordered re-investigation (vide order No. 15 dated 15.1.80). But all attempts to bring them to justice ended in failure ; probably because very influential hand came to their rescue and it succeeded in diverting the normal course of law into different channel. This is a glaring instance how innocent small fry like appellant was victimized and real culprit managed to escape trial. Mr, Yousuf (P.W. 1) himself admits that as per postal manual postmaster is to remain in custody of stamp and stationery. Another postal employee Mr. Razzaque (P.W. 4) also testified to the fact that post master is responsible for the shortage of stamps and stationery. P.W. 1 Mr. Yousuf and his predecessor Mr. Matiur Rahman remained indifferent for six years in matter of performing their duty with sincerity. But they showed gross negligence. Such a state of affair is inconceivable. The negligence of duty they have shown is in fact a criminal one. Evidence and circumstance of this case warrant inference thereof they purposely did not carry out verification of stock periodically as envisaged by Rules to screen their nefarious act of criminal misappropriation of the property Be that as it may authority concerned should better take step to bring them to justice so that ends of justice is duly vindicated and it serves as an eye opener to other responsible officers of that department. Regard being had to the legal and factual aspect of the matter. I am unerringly of opinion that prosecution has miserably failed to bring home the guilt to the appellant Abdul Majid.
